content:
When Apple finally responded to the sharp rise in memory and other component costs, its stance was quite hardline — some price hikes exceeded fifty percent, while certain memory and storage upgrades doubled in price outright.

These elevated prices are likely to persist for years, and may never come back down...

9to5Mac readers were already sceptical about whether Apple would reduce prices once component shortages eased, with more than two-thirds indicating they expected the increases to be permanent.

Subsequent analyst reports noted that supply chain pricing would not improve before 2028, and even then any improvement would be quite limited. As things stand, the current steeply raised prices look set to remain for several years at minimum, and will probably never return to previous levels.

If that turns out to be the case, how would you respond? Would you grit your teeth and continue buying Apple products at the same pace? Or would you cut back on the number or frequency of purchases? Perhaps take other measures such as buying lower-end models, opting for refurbished units, or waiting for a price drop before acting?
